ground_truth.unit: percentage points of the monthly hiring probability per percentage point of state unemployment
ground_truth.location: Table 1, Panel B, column (1), PE <= 10 x U. Rate
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Hiring Over the Business Cycle: With and Without Controls"), Panel B, column (1), row PE <= 10 x U. Rate.  Linear probability model (Equation 1 of the paper) of an indicator equal to 100 if the individual is hired in month t — begins a job at a new firm, either from non-employment in month t-1 or, if employed in t-1, reporting a change of employer since last month; new jobs classified as self-employment are not hires — on an indicator for potential experience (age minus years of education minus six) of at most ten years, and the state monthly unemployment rate interacted with each of the two potential-experience groups (at most ten years; more than ten years), with no main effect of the unemployment rate.  Column (1) has no fixed effects.  Sample: the matched monthly CPS panel, January 1994 to September 2016 (pairs of consecutive months matched on administrative IDs and confirmed on sex, race and age, following Madrian and Lefgren; May-August 1995 and month pairs spanning the eight-month sampling break excluded), civilians over 16 with non-missing age and education, all labour-force statuses in t-1.  Weighted by the average of the two months' CPS sampling weights; standard errors clustered by state (51 including DC).  The coefficient is the young workers' hiring response to one percentage point of state unemployment.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Table 1 and Table 2 hiring regressions are estimated as weighted least squares on exact weighted cell means over (state, month, demo2, young, prior labour-force status group), with cell weights equal to summed CPS weights. All regressors and fixed effects are constant within these cells, so point estimates are algebraically identical to the person-level aweighted regressions in YH_regs.do. This keeps the run inside the 300 s / 4 GB sandbox. Clustered standard errors (state) use the same meat and bread, but the (N-1)/(N-K) small-sample factor is omitted; they are printed for information only.

yh_data.csv was read in full (all 19,836,464 rows), but only the 19 columns the Table 1/2/10 specifications need (fread select=). The occupation/industry crosswalk merges are applied only to the new-hire wage sample.
deviations_stdout: hiring regressions (Tables 1-2) estimated as WLS on exact weighted cell means over (state, month, demo2, young, prior labour-force status) to fit the 300 s / 4 GB sandbox; point estimates are algebraically identical, SEs use the same clustering but the small-sample N adjustment is omitted.
cell.notes: Seeded translation of YH_data_init.do and YH_regs.do: date harmonisation, state unemployment merge, potential experience from peeduca (the CSV column for Stata's peeduc), demo2 = minority x female x hispanic x 7 education levels, hired2 (excluding self-employment) x 100, young = PE<=10, and the young/old x U-rate interactions. Sample: exp and v2unemp non-missing, giving N = 16,948,516. Table 1 cols 1 and 4 (Panels A and B) and Table 2 cols 1-4 use fixest feols with state, demo2 and month FE, fixef.rm='none', and state clustering. Table 10 Panel B col 1 is run person-level on hires with v2prwernal==0: log real weekly wage on young, youngurate and oldurate, with state, date, demo2, 2002-recoded occupation and industry FE (crosswalks merged by code-year as in the do-file). Attempts 1-5 were exploratory and printed no RESULT lines. Attempt 1 timed a column-selected fread at 168 s. Attempt 2 timed raw I/O at 101 s, then crashed on a fread argument clash. Attempt 3 found 3-thread fread slower, at 205 s. Attempts 4-5 were smoke tests on the first 2M rows with RESULT renamed TEST. The final full run took 233 s, of which 221 s was reading the file. No comparison against claimed values was followed by a script change, so there are no claim attempts.
